name: How much does a restaurant build-out cost per square foot in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: What is a realistic per-square-foot budget for a restaurant build-out in Los Angeles right now?
mainEntity.text: What is a realistic per-square-foot budget for a restaurant build-out in Los Angeles right now?

acceptedAnswer.text: A realistic budget depends on whether you are inheriting a former restaurant, a warm shell, or a cold shell. In Los Angeles, the biggest cost drivers are ventilation, grease management, plumbing, electrical upgrades, and whether the kitchen equipment can be installed without major utility upgrades. Dining room finishes can also swing the budget significantly, especially for higher-end concepts in Glendale, Pasadena, West Hollywood, or Beverly Hills. Owners should separate hard construction costs from equipment, design fees, permits, contingency, and working capital. A useful planning approach is to build a conservative low, mid, and high budget before signing a lease. That prevents a project from stalling after demolition reveals hidden issues such as damaged slab conditions, undersized utilities, or outdated mechanical systems.
acceptedAnswer.description: Restaurant build-out costs in Los Angeles vary widely by space condition and concept, but many projects fall into a broad range of roughly $200 to $400+ per square foot. A second-generation space with usable infrastructure costs less, while a first-generation shell, custom finishes, and heavy kitchen requirements push costs much higher.
